questions.question: Why do Python dictionaries preserve insertion order in Python 3.7+?

options.text: They use a compact array of entries appended sequentially plus a sparse indices table
They use an internal doubly-linked list connecting all entries
They sort keys alphabetically during every insertion
They record timestamp metadata inside PyObject

questions.explanation: PEP 468 compact dict layout separates the sparse hash index table from the dense array of entries. Keys are stored in insertion order in the dense entries array.
